epics.title: Epidemiological Material Cataloging and Management
epics.jtbd: When I have a new epidemiological protocol, I want to catalog and publish it, so that other staff can access the standardized information.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Reduce the average time to publish a new approved protocol from days to under 1 hour
requirements: R1: Define the schema for epidemiological materials including metadata like pathogen type and publication date.
R2: Authors can create, edit, and publish materials.
R3: Authors can update or unpublish existing materials.
R4: All user interfaces must comply with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility guidelines.
R5: Destructive actions like unpublish must be confirmed before they happen.
R6: Data entered in forms must survive validation errors and network issues without silent loss.

slices.title: Material Data Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing the cataloging schema for this epic, I want a structured relational model, so that materials are stored consistently.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new material draft, When it is saved, Then it is persisted with a UUID, title, content, and metadata fields.
Given a missing mandatory field, When saving, Then a constraint violation is raised.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Achieve 0% invalid metadata schema saves

slices.title: Material Management API Contract
slices.jtbd: When implementing API boundaries for this epic, I want a clear OpenAPI spec, so that backend and frontend can be built in parallel without drift.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a request to create a material, When checking the spec, Then the required fields are defined.
Given an unpublish request, When reading the spec, Then a confirmation state is required.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero integration contract breaking changes during implementation

slices.title: Material Management Backend API
slices.jtbd: When implementing the cataloging endpoints for this epic, I want to handle CRUD operations securely, so that materials can be managed.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid publish request, When received, Then the material state is updated to published.
Given a malformed payload, When received, Then a 400 error is returned with specific field errors.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Process valid CRUD requests in under 100ms

slices.title: Material Management Frontend UI
slices.jtbd: When implementing the editor UI for this epic, I want to provide a responsive and accessible editor, so that authors can comfortably manage content.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a mobile browser, When the editor opens, Then the layout adapts to the screen size without horizontal scrolling.
Given an attempted unpublish, When clicked, Then a confirmation modal is shown.
Given a form validation error, When returned from the server, Then the previously typed data remains in the form with clear contrast-compliant error labels.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero loss of user-typed data on validation failures

slices.title: Material Management QA Validation
slices.jtbd: When implementing verification for this epic, I want full coverage across the test pyramid, so that editor flows are proven to work end-to-end.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an automated E2E test, When a material is created, edited, and published, Then the content is visible to users.
Given an accessibility audit, When scanning the editor UI, Then zero WCAG 2.1 AA violations are found.
Given a simulated network failure during save, When testing resilience, Then the form data is not lost.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Maintain 95% test coverage on new material logic

epics.title: Epidemiological Knowledge Discovery and Search
epics.jtbd: When I need to respond to an outbreak, I want to quickly search and find relevant epidemiological protocols, so that I can apply the correct procedures.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Increase the successful search retrieval rate of relevant protocols to 95%
requirements: R1: Users can search for materials by text or keywords.
R2: Users can filter materials by type and pathogen.
R3: Users can view and download the selected material.
R4: All user interfaces must comply with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility guidelines.
R5: The system must provide visible feedback for search progress and empty results.

slices.title: Search Index Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing search structures for this epic, I want an optimized index schema, so that queries run efficiently.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a full-text search query, When executed, Then the database index utilizes text matching effectively.
Given a filter by pathogen type, When applied, Then the index returns results without a full table scan.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Query execution time under 50ms at P95

slices.title: Search API Contract
slices.jtbd: When implementing the search API for this epic, I want a defined contract for queries and filters, so that frontend can bind to it securely.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a search request, When reading the spec, Then pagination and filter fields are clearly typed.
Given a material detail request, When reading the spec, Then the download URL field is defined.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero drift between search frontend and backend types

slices.title: Search Backend API
slices.jtbd: When implementing search endpoints for this epic, I want to return accurate results with pagination, so that users can browse easily.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a keyword query, When the API is called, Then a paginated list of matching materials is returned.
Given a filter parameter, When applied, Then only materials matching the pathogen are returned.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Maintain API response time under 150ms

slices.title: Search Frontend UI
slices.jtbd: When implementing the search UI for this epic, I want clear feedback and responsive layout, so that users on any device can find documents.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a search operation is in progress, When waiting for results, Then a visible loading indicator is displayed.
Given a search with no matches, When it completes, Then a clear 'no results found' message is shown.
Given a mobile device, When navigating search results, Then the UI is touch-friendly and WCAG 2.1 AA compliant.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero unhandled UI states during network loading

slices.title: Search QA Validation
slices.jtbd: When implementing search tests for this epic, I want end-to-end verification, so that the critical discovery journey is proven.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an E2E test, When searching for a known keyword, Then the correct material is in the top 3 results.
Given an E2E test, When viewing a material, Then the download link successfully retrieves the file.
Given an accessibility audit, When scanning the search page, Then all form controls have visible focus and labels.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% pass rate on E2E search critical paths

epics.title: Self-Service Account Recovery
epics.jtbd: When I forget my password, I want to recover my account securely, so that I can regain access to the knowledge base without IT support.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Reduce IT support tickets for password resets to near zero
requirements: R1: Users can request a secure recovery link via email.
R2: Users can reset their password using the secure link.
R3: All interfaces must be WCAG 2.1 AA compliant.
R4: Form inputs must survive validation errors.

slices.title: Recovery API Contract
slices.jtbd: When implementing recovery boundaries for this epic, I want a secure API contract, so that token generation and validation are clearly defined.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a password reset request, When checking the spec, Then the email payload is defined.
Given a reset confirmation, When checking the spec, Then the token and new password are required.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero ambiguity in security token payload definitions

slices.title: Recovery Backend Auth API
slices.jtbd: When implementing auth recovery for this epic, I want to securely generate and validate tokens, so that accounts cannot be hijacked.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid email, When requesting a reset, Then a short-lived token is generated and emailed.
Given an expired token, When attempting to reset, Then the request is rejected with a 401 error.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero vulnerabilities in reset token lifecycle

slices.title: Recovery Frontend UI
slices.jtbd: When implementing recovery views for this epic, I want accessible forms with clear feedback, so that users can complete the reset easily.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a password mismatch error, When submitting the reset form, Then the entered password is kept and an error is shown.
Given a mobile screen, When viewing the reset page, Then the input fields are touch-friendly and contrast ratio is at least 4.5:1.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero WCAG violations on password reset forms

slices.title: Recovery QA Validation
slices.jtbd: When implementing recovery tests for this epic, I want to verify the complete reset flow, so that lockouts are dependably resolved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an E2E test, When a user requests a reset and clicks the link, Then they can successfully set a new password and log in.
Given an E2E test, When a user submits an expired token, Then the system gracefully rejects the attempt with clear UI feedback.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% test coverage on recovery token expiration and validation paths

epics.title: Automated Backups and Verified Restore
epics.jtbd: When a critical failure occurs, I want to be able to restore the knowledge base data from a backup, so that valuable epidemiological records are not lost.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Achieve a recovery time objective (RTO) of under 2 hours
epics.tocConstraintRef: Risk of data loss and downtime
requirements: R1: The system automatically backs up database and file storage daily.
R2: A verified script exists and has been tested to restore the system from backup.

slices.title: Backup Automation
slices.jtbd: When implementing backup jobs for this epic, I want automated daily snapshots, so that there is always a recent recovery point.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a production environment, When the daily schedule triggers, Then a snapshot of DB and files is pushed to secure storage.
Given a failed backup job, When it errors, Then an alert is sent to administrators.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 99.9% successful daily backup execution

slices.title: Restore Verification
slices.jtbd: When implementing restore procedures for this epic, I want a tested recovery script, so that a real disaster can be resolved quickly.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a test environment, When the restore script is executed with the latest backup, Then the system comes up with all data intact.
Given a successful test restore, When completed, Then the RTO is measured and logged.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero data loss during verified restore simulation

epics.title: Goal-Question-Metric Telemetry Foundation
epics.jtbd: When assessing system adoption, I want to measure search success and publication rates, so that I know if the platform is effectively aiding epidemiological work.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Capture 100% of defined key product actions reliably without data loss
epics.tocConstraintRef: Lack of visibility into actual product usage
requirements: R1: Goal: Ensure staff can find and utilize protocols quickly. Question: How long does a successful search take? Metric: Time from search to document view.
R2: Goal: Ensure the knowledge base stays current. Question: Are new protocols being added? Metric: Count of newly published materials per month.
R3: Goal: Ensure reliable access. Question: Are users failing to find documents? Metric: Count of zero-result searches.

slices.title: Telemetry Data Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing event storage for this epic, I want an immutable event log schema, so that metrics can be reliably queried.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an incoming telemetry event, When saved, Then it is persisted immutably with timestamp, event type, and payload.
Given a query for monthly metrics, When executed, Then it aggregates the data efficiently.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero dropped telemetry events under peak load

slices.title: Telemetry API Contract
slices.jtbd: When implementing the event API for this epic, I want a standardized schema for tracking payloads, so that frontend can report metrics reliably.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a search telemetry event, When inspecting the spec, Then latency and result count fields are required.
Given a publication event, When inspecting the spec, Then the material ID is required.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero malformed events due to contract drift

slices.title: Telemetry Backend API
slices.jtbd: When implementing event ingestion for this epic, I want a fast unauthenticated endpoint, so that tracking doesn't block the user.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid batch of events, When received by the ingestion API, Then they are processed asynchronously.
Given a malformed event, When received, Then it is discarded without crashing the service.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Event ingestion latency under 20ms

slices.title: Telemetry Frontend Dispatch
slices.jtbd: When implementing tracking for this epic, I want to dispatch events in the background, so that the UI remains fast and responsive.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a user performs a search, When results appear, Then the duration is measured and dispatched.
Given a user publishes a material, When successful, Then a publication event is dispatched.
Given a zero-result search, When it occurs, Then the query text and zero-result event are dispatched.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero main thread blocking from telemetry dispatch

slices.title: Telemetry QA Validation
slices.jtbd: When implementing telemetry tests for this epic, I want to verify accurate event capture, so that business decisions are based on real data.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an E2E test, When a full search and view journey is completed, Then the correct metrics are found in the event log.
Given an E2E test, When a material is published, Then the publication counter increments.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% accuracy in tracked event payloads during E2E simulation
